about: The five release gates of document 10 §7 and where each criterion stands. Checked by scripts/verify-acceptance.mjs: the criteria must be the specification's; a gate may be marked passed only when every criterion is met and the owner's decision is recorded; the criterion on critical defects is worked out from defects.json.

states.met: true today, with the evidence named
states.partly: part of it is true; the lines close the rest

gates.title: Design foundation
gates.needs: The owner's approval of the design on the hosted workspace (T-005). The two other open points are the agent's work.

criteria.evidence: Tokens, shell and the Reimagined theme the owner asked for (DL-017) are built and pinned by tests (`Unit/AdminDesignTokensTest.php`, `Feature/ThemeTokensTest.php`). The approval itself has not been given.

No screen shows the shared components and their states side by side. What such a screen would show exists since 20 November: the standards are written (`platform/resources/views/components/admin/README.md`), and a test draws the shared table in each of its five states (`Unit/AdminTableTest.php`).
Sidebar, top bar and phone drawer are built. On 17 November a browser opened 241 screens as four roles at 1366 px and at 390 px; none was wider than the window (`scripts/os-screens.mjs`).
Counted by tools on every screen: labels, names, one main heading, 24 px targets. No review by keyboard and by screen reader.

gates.title: Module readiness
gates.needs: Passed module by module. Each open module has its sheet in §4; the owner signs or returns it (T-171).

criteria.evidence: Documents 05 and 07 are the requirements. The schema is 109 migrations that build an empty MySQL 8.4 in CI on every push. The addresses of `/api/v1` are a contract, held by a test on every push since 19 November (document 29, `platform/resources/api/v1.openapi.json`). No module has had its requirements, its addresses and its schema approved as a set.

Unit and feature tests pass: 2,484 on 17 November, and the same suite on MySQL 8.4 in CI. In a browser both journeys and a crawl of every screen as four roles pass, by hand and, since 17 November, in CI on every push that touches the admin (`.github/workflows/vercel-livewire.yml`); which of the eleven flows of document 10 they press is in §3.

No admin address opens without a sign-in, and one role is checked against every address (`Feature/AdminRouteAccessTest.php`); the other roles are tested module by module (§4). The roles are the inherited eight, not yet the owner's matrix.

Ready for the catalogue only: 170 products, with a report that accounts for every row and every change (`docs/furniture-2030/catalogue/IMPORT-REPORT.md`). No other record has an importer. The old database holds little to move: on 17 November 1 lead, 1 client, no order, quotation or invoice.

gates.title: Puck readiness
gates.needs: The prototype of T-115. Not started; it is wave 10.

criteria.evidence: Not started. The Website Studio in the code is the HTML builder inherited from Interior; it is switched off.

criteria.text: Draft security, publish and rollback tested.

gates.title: Hostinger readiness
gates.needs: The trial site on the owner's Hostinger account: the owner's ten steps of document 24 (T-006). Everything that can be proven away from the account is proven on every change (T-143, T-144); nothing on the host can be proven before the site is there.

criteria.evidence: Verified away from the host, on every push: every migration from an empty database on MySQL 8.4, and the whole suite on MySQL 8.4, MariaDB 10.11 and MariaDB 11.4 (`.github/workflows/os-ci.yml`; Hostinger gives MariaDB under the name MySQL). Since 18 November a release as the host gets it is installed by a browser on Apache with PHP 8.4 and MariaDB 10.11 in the same workflow, and the installer's first page names every needed extension that is off (`scripts/os-install.mjs`). Not verified on the account: its PHP version and extensions, its MariaDB version, and its web server (LiteSpeed) reading the website folder's own rules.

Designed: one cron line calls the scheduler, two timed jobs drain the queue. Proven in the rehearsal on 18 November: the line the installer prints, run as it is printed and as the hosting account, starts the scheduler, and System health shows its heartbeat (`.github/workflows/os-ci.yml`, job `hostinger`). Never run on the host: the path of PHP in that line rests on what is read about Hostinger, and no queued message has left a real installation.
The Laravel admin holds no real record yet, and no backup of it has been taken or restored.

Security, on the hosted workspace: the outside check passes for the address on Vercel (`.github/workflows/vercel-live-check.yml`) and asks, since 17 November, for the Content-Security-Policy and the request number too; inside, the security tests of document 10 §4 and the content policy are pinned by tests (`tests/Feature/Security/`). Published advisories for the packages are asked of npm and Composer when a lock file changes and every week (`.github/workflows/audit.yml`); none that blocks is open. Not done: the outside check has not been pointed at Hostinger, and nothing has been measured against the plan's limits.

gates.title: Production cutover
gates.needs: The owner changes the old dashboard's password (T-021): the one open critical defect. Then gate D, and the owner's written approval of each module's move (T-181).

criteria.evidence: Given in general on 17 November: the owner lifted the holds to start a production-ready deployment (DL-022). The move of each module is approved in writing on its sheet.

No snapshot has been taken for a move. What the old database held on 17 November was read and is written down: 148 sample products, 1 lead, 1 client, 1 user, no order, quotation, invoice or payment. Since 17 November a new preview of the shop has no database; the previews built before cannot be opened without a sign-in to Vercel, and Vercel deletes them within 30 days.

Each change of 17 November has its own way back: the undo in `deploy/supabase/2026-11-17-close-data-api.sql`, the rollback file `scripts/migrations/rollback/019_catalogue.rollback.sql`, the earlier deployment kept by Vercel. A written plan for going back after a module has moved does not exist.

Both sites are asked from outside after every merge, and a timer for every six hours is in the workflow (`.github/workflows/live-check-after-merge.yml`, `.github/workflows/vercel-live-check.yml`); a failure opens an issue, proved with issue #38 on 17 November. GitHub had not yet started the timer by the evening of 17 November. Since that day every answer and every error page carries a request number, and the same number is on the log lines of that request, so a reported error can be found in the log (`tests/Feature/Observability/RequestNumberTest.php`). No error tracker, no runbook.
